In two sentences: why can a 102 GB model run on a 24 GB GPU?
Explain quantization and offloading/streaming.
A 102 GB model can run on a 24 GB GPU because the weights are typically quantized (e.g., to 4-bit
precision, cutting memory needs by ~4x) and split across memory sources, with layers or weights streamed
from CPU RAM or disk via techniques like memory-mapping or offloading. Additionally, only the active
layers need to reside in GPU memory at any moment, so frameworks like llama.cpp can compute the model
piece-by-piece at the cost of slower inference speed.
